Licences (from each file's own header, carried verbatim in `hyphdata.ts`):
en-US all-permissive (G. D. C. Kuiken); en-GB, de, fr, es, nl MIT; it and pl
dual-licensed, taken under MIT; pt BSD-3-Clause.

**Not bundled:** Russian (`hyph-ru`) is LPPL only; converting it into a generated
table is a modification LPPL conditions, so it is left out.

**Running the generator:** Node's `fetch` may time out reaching
`raw.githubusercontent.com` on a machine whose resolver prefers IPv6; run it as
`NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first npm run gen:hyph` there.

`test/fixtures/hyphenation/goldens.json` (see below) is produced by a DIFFERENT
Liang implementation, `hyphen@1.14.1` (npm, MIT, ytiurin/hyphen) over ITS OWN
bundled copy of the CTAN patterns, so agreement is evidence from outside our
engine — but not from outside the pattern data, which both ultimately share.

## Goldens

`goldens.json` is written by `scripts/gen-hyphenation-goldens.mjs` (not run by
`npm test`) from **hyphen@1.14.1**, fetched with `npm pack`, over its own bundled
pattern copy: 145 words across the nine languages, five of them French and Italian elisions.
`test/hyphenate-goldens.test.ts` compares point sets after filtering both by the
language's `hyphenmins`, since the two implementations apply their own edge
minimums. On generation (2026-10-06) every word agreed; nothing is excluded. Our side runs with the language's own minimums, `minLeft` counted from the start of an elided word's segment, which is what the oracle does (`l’uni-ver-si-tà`, not `l’u-ni-`).
Ceiling: one other implementation, and pattern data that traces back to the same
CTAN sources — this catches an engine bug, not a pattern bug.
